commit.message:
Move literal selection into the shared incremental check

The counterexample went through `check_incremental_against_fresh_after_edit`
but picked its literal itself, with a `collect_int_lits` match and a `failf`
that the property did differently (`List.nth` by seed). So the one step the two
did not share was the one they disagreed on.

The helper now takes `~literal_index`, modulo the number of literals, and does
the selection. Both call sites are a single call, matching the #2128 pair: the
property passes the generated seed, the counterexample passes 0.

Having no literal to edit is now a `no_comparison` reason rather than two
different ad-hoc handlings, so the counterexample fails with "the program has
no int literal to edit" instead of "expected exactly one int literal", and the
property keeps skipping as before.

Verified after the change: a pin input with no int literal fails on the new
guard, and one where the bug does not reproduce still fails with
"#2457 looks fixed".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Trim docstrings, rename to check_evaluator_stepper_consistent, inline the
QCheck test defs

- `check_evaluator_against_stepper` -> `check_evaluator_stepper_consistent`,
  and its comment is four lines: what it checks, and that the step limit and
  known raising issues are skipped. Dropped the `neg` explanation from both
  helpers -- that is just how `neg` works.

- Each QCheck test is defined once now, inside the `test_case` that skips it,
  rather than as a separate top-level value referenced from one place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Replace the bool return with a ~require_comparison flag

Both helpers returned "did I compare anything", which every call site then had
to handle: the properties with `ignore(...): bool`, the counterexamples with a
`check(bool, ...)` wrapper. The flag inverts that -- the helper decides, and
both return unit.

~require_comparison=false in the properties: a random draw whose reduction
does not terminate inside step_limit, or that raises from statics/evaluation,
is skipped as before.

~require_comparison=true in the counterexample tests: a fixed input that
reaches no comparison is no longer pinning anything, so it fails with which
stage stopped it and a note to re-minimize, rather than passing green.

Verified both directions with step_limit=0: the counterexample fails with
"reduction did not terminate within 0 steps, so nothing was compared", and the
property still passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Trim the comments this branch added

- Deleted the one above `testable_core_exp`; the code beneath it already said
  it renders via `QCheck_Util.show_core_exp`.
- Both helper docstrings lose a line or two of restated code. The incremental
  one also loses "both sides share one elaboration, so a disagreement is a
  reuse bug" -- the block comment above it already says that.
- The two-line comment at both `ignore` call sites is one line.
- Both "Disabled:" comments drop the trailing "which is the signal to
  re-enable this property" (the failure message says it) and, for #2128, the
  restatement of what the pin's own name says.
- `show_core_exp`'s docstring loses "Reading this is a loss of information
  either way", which was vague and said nothing.

Also fixes a pre-existing comment this branch made stale: the incremental
block comment said known skips "return `true`", but the extracted helper
reports them as `false` and the property passes on them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Share one show_core_exp between QCheck printing and Alcotest output

`show_core_exp` was defined twice: once local to `QCheck_Util.arb_exp` as the
generator's printer, once at the top of Test_Evaluator_Properties feeding the
Alcotest testable. Hoisted the QCheck_Util one to a top-level and built
`testable_core_exp` on it, so QCheck counterexamples and Alcotest failures read
alike.

The two copies did not agree, and the properties' copy was the worse of the
two. It used `of_core(~inline=true, CoreSettings.off)`, whose Evaluation.init
sets show_ascriptions = false and show_fn_bodies = false, so casts are hidden
and function bodies folded -- two expressions that `Equality.semantic` counts
as different can print identically, which is the confusion #2408 describes.
`editable` shows both, so the surviving definition is that one.

Rendering-only: no equality or pass/fail behaviour changes. Also drops the
now-unused `open Haz3lcore` from Test_Evaluator_Properties.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Use Alcotest's neg instead of a hand-rolled verdict type

The `verdict` type, `holds` and `check_still_fails` are gone. Alcotest already
has the primitive for this: `neg : 'a testable -> 'a testable`, a testable with
negated equality.

So there is now one parameterized check per property, taking the `testable` and
`msg` that `Alcotest.check` would take anyway:

  check_evaluator_against_stepper(~step_limit, ~testable, ~msg, uexp)
  check_incremental_against_fresh_after_edit(~target_id, ~old_value, ~testable, ~msg, exp)

The property passes `testable_core_exp`; the counterexample passes
`neg(testable_core_exp)` and a message naming the property to re-enable. Same
function, same comparison, opposite expectation -- and on failure Alcotest
renders both expressions itself, which is why `testable_core_exp` is back.

Each returns whether it actually compared anything, so a counterexample that
stops reaching a result is reported as needing re-minimizing rather than
silently passing. The properties discard that answer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Address review: shared verdict type, drop invented terminology, trim comments

- Neither helper returns an option any more. Both produce a `verdict`
  (`Holds` / `Fails(rendered)` / `Vacuous`), so the comparison lives inside
  the shared function instead of being repeated by each caller. `holds` reads
  a verdict as a QCheck predicate; `check_still_fails` reads it as a
  counterexample pinning a known bug.

- Dropped "engine", which the codebase doesn't use.
  `reduce_both_engines` -> `evaluator_and_stepper_agree`, matching the
  property's own name; `eval_after_literal_edit` ->
  `incremental_agrees_with_fresh_after_edit`.

- The pins' long comments are gone. Each disabled property now sits next to
  its own `..._disabled` wrapper and carries one comment: the known bug, its
  issue URL, and that the test below is the signal to re-enable. The `tests`
  list is bare, so nothing is said twice.

- Failure messages carry the issue URL rather than a bare number.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: disable two seed-flaky evaluator properties, pin them as expected failures

`Evaluator.Properties` case 5 ("Evaluator and stepper are consistent") and
case 7 ("Incremental eval agrees with fresh eval after a literal edit") both
fail whenever QCheck happens to draw the shape that trips a known open bug.
Since #2422 made the runner propagate a real exit status, that reddens Full
tests on unrelated PRs -- runs 33513972427, 33513747011 and 33412342909 all
died on case 7 alone.

Both are disabled the same way as the existing "Preservation of types"
property: a `test_case` that calls `Alcotest.skip()` and still references the
QCheck test, so the property keeps compiling and is trivial to re-enable.

In place of each, a deterministic unit test pins the known counterexample:

- #2128/#2372: `fun (x::x) -> x`, where one engine freshens the duplicate
  binder and the other does not.
- #2457: `{ let x = (); let _ = 4; let true = A }` with the literal bumped,
  where fresh eval substitutes `x` into the residual and incremental eval
  leaves it a variable.

These assert the current, wrong behaviour rather than calling
`Alcotest.skip()` like `skip_known_bug` elsewhere in test/. A skipped test
stays silent forever; these go red the day the bug is fixed and name the
property to re-enable.

To keep each pin honest, the shared work is extracted rather than duplicated:
`reduce_both_engines` runs both engines, `eval_after_literal_edit` runs the
one-literal-edit experiment, and both the property and its pin call it.

Viewport culling measured the first .code-container and applied the
range to every cell. Drv scratchpads no longer report culling support,

visible_rows on the predicate, and cells can opt out (CellEditor ~cull)

commit.message:
Functorize SliderProj / SliderFProj over the literal they edit

The two were 63 lines each and 52 lines identical -- the entire difference was
Bigint vs float: which atom they read, which atom they build, and how they
render. SliderCore.Make now holds the shared body and each variant supplies
only that difference, 14-16 lines apiece.

Atom.t is the natural seam: both projectors were matching
`Exp({term: Atom(Int(i)), _})` / `Atom(Float(f))` and rebuilding the same way,
so PARAMS asks for of_atom / to_atom / to_string and nothing else.

Net -17 lines, which undersells it -- the point is that a change to slider
behaviour is now one edit rather than two that can drift apart.

Failure message wording is preserved ("Slider: Get: not integer literal",
"SliderF: Put: not float literal") via a separate `literal` label, rather than
being degraded to the module name. ProjectorInit.re:12-13 references
SliderProj.M / SliderFProj.M and is unchanged.

make test-quick: 3225 passing. dev, test and release builds clean.

commit.message:
ci: drive the split by trigger instead of by conditionals

The previous shape had four jobs across two workflows and six guards: three
job-level gh-readonly-queue checks, and three step-level `merge_group ||
fork` guards on gates that were defined twice, once per workflow. The
duplication existed because `deploy.yml` ran on `push`, which a fork cannot
fire, so `ci.yml` had to repeat every gate for the cases `push` misses.

Restructured so each filter is a trigger rather than an `if:`:

    checks.yml    on: workflow_call        the definitions, one copy
                  Fast checks    fmt + make ci-check + make ci-quick
                  Full tests     make ci + Test Report + Codecov

    ci.yml        on: push (branches-ignore gh-readonly-queue/**)
                      | merge_group
    fork-ci.yml   on: pull_request, if: ...head.repo.fork
    deploy.yml    on: push (branches-ignore gh-readonly-queue/**)
                  Deploy branch preview

Two conditionals remain: the fork `if:`, and a publish-reports input that
turns off the Test Report check runs and the Codecov upload for forks, whose
GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only and which get no secrets.

`ci.yml` deliberately has no `pull_request` trigger. A same-repo pull
request fires both it and `push` for one commit, so the full suite would run
twice. Forks are the only case `push` cannot see, and fork-ci.yml covers
them; 3 of the last 200 PRs here came from forks, and none of them get CI
today, so this is not a regression.

Both `ci.yml` triggers are load-bearing. A merge queue does push its
gh-readonly-queue/** branch, but Actions only reports status into the queue
from a `merge_group` run -- so the trigger makes the queue's checks exist
and branches-ignore stops the same commit being checked twice, and stops a
speculative merge being published as a preview.

Formatting, warnings and the quick suite share one job on purpose. Each
extra job re-installs the toolchain (~2 min warm, 5-9 min cold), which costs
more than the work those checks do. `Fast checks`, `Full tests` and the
deploy are three independent jobs with no `needs:`, so each re-runs alone.

`Build release` is no longer a separate gate; the deploy job runs the same
command. That leaves src/web's main and worker jsoo executables unlinked on
fork PRs and in the merge queue, which we're accepting until it bites.

Part of #2203. Closes #2456.

commit.message:
menhir: () is an atomic pattern (replaces the point patches)

The editor treats () as an atomic pattern constituent with no
positional restrictions; the menhir grammar instead listed UNIT at
hand-picked spots (whole parameter, ascribed parameter, cons chain
after the last fix) and every unlisted position was a parse error —
fun (), x -> x was still broken. UNIT now lives in nonAscriptingPat
like every other atom and the four point productions are deleted.
Net conflict count DROPS vs both the point-patched and pre-fix
grammars (55 s/r + 2 r/r states vs 59+4 and 57+2). Pins added for the
comma-element and constructor-argument positions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

menhir: () legal inside fun-parameter cons chains

MenhirFuzz (seed 42) found fun ?:: () -> ... deterministically
rejected by menhir while the editor parser accepts it: funConsPat
built only from nonAscriptingPat, which has no UNIT — () was legal as
a whole parameter but not as a cons operand (head or tail). UNIT is
now inlined at both chain positions (not factored into an operand
nonterminal, which costs 4 mixed-action r/r states; inlining adds only
2 identical-action r/r states, documented in the known-conflict list).
Pinned: unit tail/head/both, the fuzz counterexample, unit mid-chain.
Pinning also surfaced a PRE-EXISTING divergence recorded as a skip
case: on 'fun x :: y : [T] ->' MakeTerm ascribes the last element,
menhir the whole chain — needs its own decision.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Probes: empty lists are no evidence for auto-rich rendering

An empty list parses as an empty card hand, so auto-rich probes were
rendering unrelated empty lists ([] of Int) as empty-hand silhouettes.
Auto paths now require a non-vacuous match: the probe-level gate and the
per-sample pick accept evidence from any sibling sample at the site, so
card probes with mixed streams keep their empty-hand silhouettes, while
sites that only ever observe [] show plain text. Explicit renderer
picks (^^card, the View-as menu) are unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Cards: never hide the caret beside a card projector; top-anchor cards

The 'turn off caret when focused' rule made the caret invisible at the
positions directly left/right of a card (.indicated covers adjacency,
not just interaction) — walking the caret through a card made it vanish.
Cards also rendered centered on their line here (the tab-extent wrapper
that top-anchors them elsewhere isn't on this branch): align-items
flex-start anchors the card-wrapper so cards dip below the line.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Cards doc slide: probed sorting section; shorter Rich Views tooltip

The cards slide gains insertion sort and quicksort over Hands with
probes on the interesting lines — with Rich Views on (the default),
every intermediate hand renders as actual cards, including the
empty-hand silhouettes at the base cases. A comment in the slide
points at the toggle and the per-sample double-click.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Offside stagger: multi-row displays clear code and each other

An after-display pass (ProbeStagger, precedent RefractorShift) measures
each offside wrapper from the DOM, floors its x at the end of every
code line it spans (Measured row max_cols), and first-fits it into the
leftmost gap among displays already placed by rows above — it slides
BEFORE a higher display when the overhang up there leaves room, and
past it otherwise. Positions patch pre-paint; the single-row
no-collision case reproduces the base offside position exactly, so
nothing moves unless staggering demands it. Rich card fans among dense
probes stop overlapping program text and one another.

Ported from agent-canvas rounds 43-44.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Rich probes: render inside the sample chip; global Rich Views default

Rich content embeds within the .value chip — inert, so the chip keeps
every sample interaction (dropdown with Hide, capture, dbl-click
toggles, shift-drag resize) and the green backing centers its content
as a flex box. The anchored modal is retired: explicit activations
that fit inline_rows_cap (4) embed in the row; taller content
auto-opens the drawer on activation. Many mode renders one card/fan
per sample chip.

A Rich Views toggle (probes sidebar, default ON) auto-embeds the first
applicable renderer for any probe when the content fits the cap;
per-probe double-click opts back to text (rich_off). Tables stay
opt-in. ProbeProj.standalone_rich renders one value outside any probe
(for aggregate displays).

Ported from agent-canvas rounds 38-45.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Cards: forward-port to the reworked RichProbe API + empty hands + centering

CardRenderer gains the `empty` model and `drawer_rows` the registry
rework requires. An empty hand renders a card-footprint silhouette
(dotted outline, circled ∅) in both the projector and the rich view —
previously it rendered as nothing. Fan geometry matches CardProj's, and
the empty case reserves one card width.

Ported from agent-canvas rounds 39/44/45.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add card RichProbe renderer for probed values

Reintroduce the card rich-probe (reverted in 279a0e9672) so probed
runtime values matching the card or hand shape can be opened in the
probe sidebar modal as a card visualization, alongside the existing
inline CardProj projector.

Refactor card code into shared CardTypes / CardSyntax / CardView so the
inline projector and the rich-probe renderer share types, syntax
conversions, and the spritesheet view. CardView.Chooser.view is
parameterized by an ~on_pick callback so each consumer wires picking to
its own mutation pathway: CardProj keeps its per-card-in-hand chooser
via ReplaceCardInHand; CardRenderer does whole-expression replacement
via card_to_exp + SetSyntax. Rich-probe Hand is display-only (no
chooser), Singleton has the chooser. Tolerant model_of_sexp falls back
to {mode: Show} on unknown variants.

Modal-context CSS pins .projector.card to position:relative (the
.projector base is absolute, which collapsed the modal to 0x0 and made
the close button overlap the cards) and strips the modal's
background/shadow/radius when it contains a card so the sprites aren't
framed by a redundant panel. Hand.view sets an explicit width on .hand
so the modal sizes correctly when its children are absolutely
positioned.
